project_type: Next.js 16 (App Router) + TypeScript booking/payments SaaS for influencer sessions, with a separate BullMQ worker process
build_system: npm scripts. Prisma 7 client is generated to ./generated/prisma (output in prisma/schema.prisma generator block). Path alias @/* -> ./* (tsconfig).
test_framework: node:test run via tsx (`tsx --test tests/*.test.ts`). Existing tests: slots.test.ts and signature.test.ts are pure/unit (no DB); holds.test.ts and payments.test.ts need a live Postgres per README.
build_command: npm run build (next build). NOTE: not runnable in this sandbox, see environment_constraints.
test_command: npm test (tsx --test tests/*.test.ts). NOTE: not runnable in this sandbox, see environment_constraints.
verification_instructions: In a normal environment: `npm install`, `npx prisma generate`, `npm run typecheck` (tsc --noEmit), `npm run build`, `npm test`, and `npm run db:migrate` against a live Postgres. In THIS sandbox none of these run (registry blocked). Validate instead by: (1) reading each new/changed file for TypeScript correctness and consistency with existing patterns; (2) grep-based structural checks (imports resolve to real exports, Prisma field names match schema, enum values match); (3) confirming new Prisma schema fields have a matching SQL migration; (4) confirming no runtime file imports a symbol that does not exist. State clearly in the final report which checks were static-only.
snapshot_or_generated_files: generated/prisma is produced by `prisma generate` from prisma/schema.prisma; it is gitignored and NOT checked in. Prisma migrations under prisma/migrations/ ARE checked in and must be added by hand here (prisma migrate dev cannot run without a DB). Match the existing hand-written SQL migration style in prisma/migrations/20261009000000_google_meet/migration.sql.
setup_instructions: Normally: start Postgres + Redis, copy .env.example to .env and fill secrets, `npm install`, `npx prisma migrate dev`, `npm run db:seed`, `npm run dev`, and `npm run worker` in a second terminal. generate TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY and APP_SECRET with `openssl rand -base64 32`.
environment_constraints: Network mode INTEGRATIONS_ONLY. The public npm registry returns 403 Forbidden: `npm install`, `npx`, and `prisma generate` all FAIL. node_modules contains only ~36K of empty placeholder dirs (no real packages, no .bin, no tsc). Therefore the coder CANNOT run npm install, typecheck, next build, prisma generate, prisma migrate, or the test runner. There is also no reachable Postgres, Redis, Google, Razorpay, or SMTP. Do NOT attempt `npm install` or long registry fetches (they hang ~2min then 403). Implement in source and validate by inspection + grep. Write unit tests anyway (they will run in CI where deps exist); keep new unit tests DB-free and pure where possible, following tests/slots.test.ts and tests/signature.test.ts.
contribution_requirements: No CONTRIBUTING.md. Conventions observed: TypeScript strict; errors modeled as named Error subclasses thrown from lib/ and mapped to HTTP status in route handlers; zod for request body validation; all times stored UTC; secrets/signatures via node:crypto; signed expiring links via lib/signing.ts (signToken/verifyToken with a per-purpose string); alerts via lib/alerts.ts structured-log sender (Phase 4 messaging/SMS/email NOT implemented yet, so use the same log-sender pattern rather than real delivery); Prisma access through lib/db.ts singleton; capacity/seat races guarded by SELECT ... FOR UPDATE inside prisma.$transaction (see lib/holds.ts and lib/checkout.ts). Commit in logical commits on branch phase-6-groups-and-dashboard. Do NOT push or open a PR.
key_patterns: createMeetingForBooking in lib/meeting.ts is the heart of event creation: it is idempotent, derives the Calendar event id from the booking id (calendarEventId), adds the single customer as attendee, polls for the Meet link, then marks the booking SCHEDULED and enqueues the confirmation message. Phase 6 must make GROUP services share ONE event per Session: derive the event id from the session, create it once (first paid attendee), then PATCH the event to add each subsequent paid attendee, and copy the same meetLink/eventId onto every booking in that session. lib/google.ts is a hand-rolled fetch client (GoogleClient interface) with insertEvent/getEvent and classified errors (GoogleReconnectError/TransientError/RequestError); it needs a patchEvent/updateAttendees method and support for multiple attendees. Seat counting is already transactional in lib/holds.ts (activeSeatWhere + FOR UPDATE on the session row) and respects service.capacity for groups. There is NO dashboard, NO Message model, NO blocked-dates concept, NO email, and NO auth yet; the connect flow authorises via a signed link (lib/google-tokens.ts buildConnectUrl) and the doc says the dashboard replaces it.
